items.coder_A: EGFR mutation/amplification is an entry requirement for verteporfin, but the record states no mechanistic link between verteporfin and EGFR; match status could change the primary outcome.
items.reason: "Eligible participants have tumors that show mutant or amplified EGFR" is an entry requirement. Verteporfin is not an EGFR inhibitor, though, and the record gives only "tumor cells which may be sensitive to verteporfin" with no stated EGFR mechanism. The design deliberately pairs the drug with EGFR+ GBM (title), so a link may be implied.

items.coder_B: EGFR mutation/amplification is an entry requirement and is in the title, but the record states no mechanistic link between EGFR and verteporfin (not an EGFR inhibitor).
items.reason: Same item as Coder A's flag. The record names EGFR selection ("Recurrent High Grade EGFR-Mutated Glioblastoma") but gives no mechanistic link to verteporfin.

note: This decides the primary outcome. The manual requires a mechanistic link, and the record states none, so I proposed false. But the whole trial is built around EGFR-mutant or amplified GBM for verteporfin, so XL or the clinical co-author should decide whether a design-implied link counts as candidate-matched.
